import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';

/**
 * `c_maxOrderQuantity` is a Zimmermann-custom SFCC attribute — a real BM site preference
 * (Integer, default 3, min 1, per-site) surfaced onto the SCAPI product response via a
 * `dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` hook, per Confluence `TSD-SFCC-268` (406913046). It has no
 * typed field on the base SDK's `Product` type — it only reaches this shape via that type's own
 * `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, the same situation
 * `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` lines 16-23 document for a
 * different custom attribute (`c_productBadges`). Narrowed here to a local type rather than
 * trusting `any` at the call site, per AGENTS.md's Gotchas: "Commerce SDK types not importable
 * ... declare a narrow local type."
 *
 * Typed `unknown`, not `number | undefined`: this function's whole job is validating a value
 * that may legitimately arrive absent, as `0`, negative, or non-numeric (see the pass criteria
 * this file's own test covers) — typing it as `number | undefined` would assert a guarantee the
 * real BM data doesn't have.
 *
 * As of this commit `TSD-SFCC-268` is still `v0.1 Draft` (Technical Lead sign-off Pending) and a
 * live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — the `afterGET` hook is
 * not deployed yet. Reading the field with the fallback below degrades to today's hardcoded
 * behaviour while that remains true, and picks up the real per-site value the day the hook ships,
 * with no further frontend change needed.
 */
type ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
  c_maxOrderQuantity?: unknown;
};

/**
 * Frontend fallback when no valid `c_maxOrderQuantity` is present. Matches
 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s own `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` value (3) exactly
 * (see that file's lines 124-125: "Frontend-enforced limit (SFCC-196). SFCC has no platform
 * max-order-quantity field."), but is deliberately its own, independent constant rather than a
 * shared/promoted one — the TSD's resolution order is product override (SFCC-703) -> site
 * preference -> this hardcoded value, so a constant shared between the PDP and this cart-facing
 * util would need reworking the day the real per-site preference ships anyway.
 */
const DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY = 3;

/**
 * Reads the real per-product order-quantity cap off a SCAPI product response
 * (`c_maxOrderQuantity`), falling back to `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` when the attribute is
 * absent or not a valid, usable cap (zero, negative, or non-numeric) — see this file's own
 * module docblock for why a shared constant is deliberately not used here.
 *
 * @param product A SCAPI product response (or product-shaped object) that may carry
 * `c_maxOrderQuantity`.
 * @returns The product's real max order quantity, or `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` (3) when no
 * valid value is present.
 */
export const getMaxOrderQuantity = (product: ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity): number => {
  const value = product?.c_maxOrderQuantity;
  return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? value : DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY;
};

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	import { OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED } from 'app/components/ui-kits/zimmCartItemShared';
3	
4	/** State the component feeds in so the recipe can resolve the value display's dimmed state.
5	 *  Named `disabled` (not e.g. `isUnavailable`) to match the resolution-prop convention already
6	 *  used by every other function-form baseStyle in this codebase (zimmTextInput.css.ts's own
7	 *  `disabled` key) — `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s PROP_COMBINATIONS harness only
8	 *  exercises the fixed key set `{inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled}`, so a
9	 *  differently-named boolean here would never have its `true` branch walked by that guard. */
10	export type ZimmQuantityStepperStyleProps = {
11	  disabled?: boolean;
12	};
13	
14	/**
15	 * Recipe — cart-line quantity stepper (SFCC-271). Two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls sit
16	 * either side of a numeric value display; all hover/press/focus/disabled states for the buttons
17	 * themselves live entirely in zimmButton.css.ts (untouched by this file — see index.tsx, which
18	 * composes ZimmButton rather than restyling it).
19	 *
20	 * `root` — the flex row. Gap is 8px (`var(--zimm-scale-xs)` — foundation/spacing.ts's `xs` is
21	 * `0.5rem`/8px exactly, so this needs no new token). Deliberate, disclosed departure from
22	 * Figma's own raw annotation, which shows a 12px gap around a bare 12px glyph with no drawn
23	 * touch target at all. ZimmButton's `icon` size variant already resolves both buttons to a 24px
24	 * touch target (zimmButton.css.ts `sizes.icon` — `minW`/`minH`: `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, cited
25	 * there against WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8, and matching the Figma node's own literal name
26	 * `touchTarget` at value 24) — i.e. 6px of invisible padding is already added on every side of
27	 * each 12px glyph before this gap is even applied. An 8px authored gap between the two 24px
28	 * button boxes therefore reproduces the ~12px glyph-to-glyph spacing Figma's raw annotation
29	 * intended (6px inset + 8px gap + 6px inset from centre-of-glyph to centre-of-glyph ≈ the
30	 * annotated 12px), without shrinking either button below its accessible 24px target — the
31	 * alternative (an 8px gap measured glyph-edge to glyph-edge with no inset accounted for) would
32	 * under-space them relative to Figma; this recipe's 8px is the touch-target-aware equivalent,
33	 * not a straight copy of the raw annotation.
34	 *
35	 * `value` — the numeric display. No Figma node or type-style was supplied for this specific text
36	 * in this build step; `body2Strong` (14px / 500 weight / 18px line-height, typography.ts) is the
37	 * nearest existing textStyle — PROVISIONAL pending UI-designer confirmation, same disclosure
38	 * pattern as zimmSizeSelector.css.ts's own oneSize label. Dims to OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED when
39	 * `disabled` (the whole control is OOS/unavailable, not just one bound) — sourced from
40	 * zimmCartItemShared.ts rather than restated here or imported from zimmButton.css.ts, so the
41	 * value display and the two buttons beside it (which get their own dimming entirely from
42	 * zimmButton.css.ts's `icon` variant, once the caller passes `ariaDisabled` through — nothing
43	 * about that is duplicated here) can never visually drift apart, without this recipe reaching
44	 * into an unrelated atom's styling module for the number. Applying the SAME opacity to `root`
45	 * as well would double it up on the buttons (0.4 × 0.4 = 0.16, not 0.4) — deliberately scoped to
46	 * `value` only for that reason.
47	 */
48	export const ZimmQuantityStepper = {
49	  parts: ['root', 'value'],
50	  baseStyle: ({ disabled }: ZimmQuantityStepperStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
51	    root: {
52	      display: 'inline-flex',
53	      alignItems: 'center',
54	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
55	    },
56	    value: {
57	      display: 'inline-flex',
58	      alignItems: 'center',
59	      justifyContent: 'center',

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED } from 'app/components/ui-kits/zimmCartItemShared';

/** State the component feeds in so the recipe can resolve the value display's dimmed state.
 *  Named `disabled` (not e.g. `isUnavailable`) to match the resolution-prop convention already
 *  used by every other function-form baseStyle in this codebase (zimmTextInput.css.ts's own
 *  `disabled` key) — `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s PROP_COMBINATIONS harness only
 *  exercises the fixed key set `{inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled}`, so a
 *  differently-named boolean here would never have its `true` branch walked by that guard. */
export type ZimmQuantityStepperStyleProps = {
  disabled?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Recipe — cart-line quantity stepper (SFCC-271). Two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls sit
 * either side of a numeric value display; all hover/press/focus/disabled states for the buttons
 * themselves live entirely in zimmButton.css.ts (untouched by this file — see index.tsx, which
 * composes ZimmButton rather than restyling it).
 *
 * `root` — the flex row. Gap is 8px (`var(--zimm-scale-xs)` — foundation/spacing.ts's `xs` is
 * `0.5rem`/8px exactly, so this needs no new token). Deliberate, disclosed departure from
 * Figma's own raw annotation, which shows a 12px gap around a bare 12px glyph with no drawn
 * touch target at all. ZimmButton's `icon` size variant already resolves both buttons to a 24px
 * touch target (zimmButton.css.ts `sizes.icon` — `minW`/`minH`: `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, cited
 * there against WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8, and matching the Figma node's own literal name
 * `touchTarget` at value 24) — i.e. 6px of invisible padding is already added on every side of
 * each 12px glyph before this gap is even applied. An 8px authored gap between the two 24px
 * button boxes therefore reproduces the ~12px glyph-to-glyph spacing Figma's raw annotation
 * intended (6px inset + 8px gap + 6px inset from centre-of-glyph to centre-of-glyph ≈ the
 * annotated 12px), without shrinking either button below its accessible 24px target — the
 * alternative (an 8px gap measured glyph-edge to glyph-edge with no inset accounted for) would
 * under-space them relative to Figma; this recipe's 8px is the touch-target-aware equivalent,
 * not a straight copy of the raw annotation.
 *
 * `value` — the numeric display. No Figma node or type-style was supplied for this specific text
 * in this build step; `body2Strong` (14px / 500 weight / 18px line-height, typography.ts) is the
 * nearest existing textStyle — PROVISIONAL pending UI-designer confirmation, same disclosure
 * pattern as zimmSizeSelector.css.ts's own oneSize label. Dims to OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED when
 * `disabled` (the whole control is OOS/unavailable, not just one bound) — sourced from
 * zimmCartItemShared.ts rather than restated here or imported from zimmButton.css.ts, so the
 * value display and the two buttons beside it (which get their own dimming entirely from
 * zimmButton.css.ts's `icon` variant, once the caller passes `ariaDisabled` through — nothing
 * about that is duplicated here) can never visually drift apart, without this recipe reaching
 * into an unrelated atom's styling module for the number. Applying the SAME opacity to `root`
 * as well would double it up on the buttons (0.4 × 0.4 = 0.16, not 0.4) — deliberately scoped to
 * `value` only for that reason.
 */
export const ZimmQuantityStepper = {
  parts: ['root', 'value'],
  baseStyle: ({ disabled }: ZimmQuantityStepperStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
    root: {
      display: 'inline-flex',
      alignItems: 'center',
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
    },
    value: {
      display: 'inline-flex',
      alignItems: 'center',
      justifyContent: 'center',
      textStyle: 'body2Strong',
      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
      opacity: disabled ? OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED : 1,
    },
  }),
};

Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (branch feature/SFCC-11_cart — do not switch branches, do not commit, do not edit `overrides/app/components/product-item/index.tsx` or `overrides/app/components/product-item/index.test.tsx` — those two files are the subject under test and have already been verified separately; you are only observing behavior, never modifying them).

CONTEXT: A cart line-item component was just changed to render `ZimmQuantityStepper` (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx`) instead of an old, buggy quantity picker. The molecule renders:
```tsx
<chakra.span __css={styles.value} aria-live="polite">
  {quantity}
</chakra.span>
```
between two buttons with real accessible names `'Decrease quantity'` / `'Increase quantity'`. The OLD component's known, already-fixed bug was that its screen-reader announcement captured a value ONCE and never re-read it on change — so it looked accessible (had a live region) but never actually announced updates. Your job is to PROVE, with a real interaction against real rendered output, that the NEW component's live region genuinely updates its DOM text content after a real click — not just that the `aria-live="polite"` attribute is present in markup. A markup-only check would not have caught the original bug and must not be treated as proof here.

ENVIRONMENT ALREADY CONFIRMED WORKING FOR YOU:
- Storybook dev server is live at `http://localhost:6006` (confirmed serving current code).
- Target story: `Commerce/ProductItem`, `Default` export. Its iframe URL is `http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=commerce-productitem--default&viewMode=story`.
- That story's mock product starts at `quantity: 1`, has no `c_maxOrderQuantity` (so the real cap resolves to a fallback of 3 via `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`), and its `onItemQuantityChange` arg is a Storybook `fn(async () => true)` — i.e. it always resolves `true`. Storybook renders through the REAL, unmocked `useDerivedProduct` hook (a real `useState`-backed quantity, confirmed by reading `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product.js`), so a real click on Increment should cause a REAL state update and re-render, visibly changing the displayed number from 1 to 2.
- `playwright-core` is installed and resolvable from the project root (`require('playwright-core')` from a script run with cwd `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`), and a Chromium binary is already downloaded (`~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium-1223`) — `chromium.launch()` should work without needing to download anything. Do not modify `playwright.config.*` (Tier 1, frozen) — this is a standalone ad hoc script, not part of the configured E2E suite; write it to your scratchpad directory and run it with plain `node`, not through any Playwright test runner or config.

YOUR TASK:
1. Write a small Node script (in your scratchpad dir) using `playwright-core`'s `chromium.launch()` to open the iframe URL above in a real browser.
2. Locate the increment button by accessible name (`'Increase quantity'`) and the aria-live value span (it's the `<span>` between the two buttons carrying `aria-live="polite"` — you can locate it via `page.locator('span[aria-live="polite"]')` or by its visible text). Grab a persistent handle/locator to that exact span (not a fresh query each time) so you can prove the SAME DOM node's content changed, not that a new node with different text appeared.
3. Record its exact `textContent` BEFORE any interaction (expect `'1'`).
4. Click the real increment button. Wait for the async chain to settle (the click triggers `product-item/index.tsx`'s `handleStepperQuantityChange`, which does `Promise.resolve(onItemQuantityChange(nextQuantity)).then(...)` before committing — give it a real wait, e.g. `page.waitForFunction(...)` polling the span's text, not an arbitrary fixed sleep if you can avoid it, but a short explicit wait is fine if needed).
5. Record the SAME span handle's `textContent` AFTER the click (expect `'2'`). This before/after pair on the same node is your core proof.
6. Repeat once more (click increment again, expect `'3'`), then click increment a third time and confirm the value stays at `'3'` (the fallback max cap) and that the increment button now carries `aria-disabled="true"`.
7. Click decrement once and confirm the value goes back down (from `'3'` to `'2'`), proving both directions genuinely update the live region, not just increment.
8. Capture and report any browser console errors or page errors during the whole sequence (`page.on('console')`, `page.on('pageerror')`).
9. Close the browser cleanly.

If, for any environment reason, launching Chromium or reaching Storybook fails, report the EXACT error text, then fall back to a real-hook-chain Vitest proof instead: `overrides/app/components/product-item/index.stories.test.tsx` already has a `renderWithStoryProviders` helper that renders `ProductItem` through the real, unmocked `useDerivedProduct` (confirm by reading that file first — it explains exactly what's mocked and why, and none of the mocks affect quantity/live-region behavior). Write a throwaway test using that same provider pattern, passing a real `onItemQuantityChange={async () => true}`, `fireEvent.click` the real increment button, and after `await waitFor(...)` read the live-region span's `textContent` directly (not just `getByText` — you want to prove the actual text changed, ideally by capturing the same DOM node reference before and after). Do NOT save this into the real `index.stories.test.tsx` or `index.test.tsx` files — write it as a new temp file inside `overrides/app/components/product-item/` (e.g. `index.tmpLiveRegionProbe.test.tsx`), run it once with `npx vitest run <that path>`, then DELETE the temp file when done and confirm via `git status --short overrides/app/components/product-item/` that nothing stray is left behind.

REPORT BACK: the real observed textContent values at each step (not what you expect, what you actually saw), whether the SAME DOM node was confirmed to change (not a node swap), any console/page errors, and a clear CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE verdict on whether the live region genuinely re-announces on real, live-hook-driven quantity changes. Also explicitly state which method you used (live Playwright-against-Storybook, or the Vitest fallback) and why.

import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * State the component feeds in so this recipe can resolve the Item Details gap widening for an
 * active error-variant ZimmInlineMessage (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Named `hasError` (not
 * e.g. `isError`/`errorActive`) to match the resolution-prop convention already used by every
 * other function-form baseStyle in this codebase — zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts's own `disabled`
 * key, and that file's own comment on why: theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts's
 * PROP_COMBINATIONS harness only exercises the fixed key set `{inverse, disabled, hasError,
 * focused, filled}`, so a differently-named boolean here would never have its `true` branch
 * walked by that guard.
 */
export type ZimmCartItemStyleProps = {
  hasError?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Co-located recipe for the cart line-item shell (overrides/app/components/product-item).
 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2) — restyles the copy-first port to the Figma-sourced cart-item spec.
 *
 * Parts:
 *   - `row` — the image + item-details row. Figma: gap 28px desktop / 24px mobile, align
 *     centre desktop / start mobile.
 *   - `details` — the column beside the image (name/attrs/price/stepper/actions). Figma:
 *     gap 12px desktop / 24px mobile.
 *   - `info` — the name + colour/size (+ mobile price) block, paired with the desktop-only
 *     delivery-actions slot. Figma: column layout desktop / row + justify-space-between
 *     mobile. The mobile values match this block's pre-existing unconditional layout exactly
 *     (row, space-between, align flex-end) so nothing changes below `md` — only the desktop
 *     column switch is new.
 *
 * Applied via `sx`, not `__css`, though the two parts of this file's `Flex`/`Stack` pair get
 * there for different reasons — corrected here (round 2 rework) after reading both chunks
 * directly rather than assuming they behave alike:
 *   - `Stack` (`chunk-WKZT7ZXJ.mjs`) passes its own computed `alignItems`/`justifyContent`/
 *     `flexDirection`/`gap` as SEPARATE literal props ahead of `{...rest}` in its own render
 *     (`jsx(chakra.div, {..., alignItems: align, ..., gap: spacing, ...rest})`). Those land in
 *     `@chakra-ui/system`'s `toCSSObject` (`chunk-E32MZNBA.mjs`) `styleProps` tier —
 *     `assignAfter({}, __css, baseStyle, styleProps, sx)` — which sits ABOVE `__css`, so a
 *     `__css`-applied value from this recipe would be silently outranked by Stack's own `gap`
 *     whenever this component also sets one. `sx` (last, unconditionally winning) avoids that.
 *   - `Flex` (`chunk-MPFPK3CX.mjs`) does NOT do the same thing — it does not pass `align`/
 *     `justify`/`direction` as separate literal props at all. It bundles all of them into ONE
 *     `__css` object, placed BEFORE `{...rest}` (`jsx(chakra.div, {ref, __css: styles, ...rest})`).
 *     That is the same silent-full-object-discard mechanism `item-variant.css.ts`'s own docblock
 *     documents for `Text` — a later same-named key in one object literal replaces the earlier
 *     one, it does not merge — just with the winner reversed: a caller-supplied `__css` prop
 *     arriving via `rest` would silently discard Flex's OWN align/justify/direction/etc
 *     translation entirely, not the other way around. `sx` is a different prop name, so it never
 *     collides with either `__css` at this level — it flows through `rest` untouched and is
 *     merged in later, last, by the same `toCSSObject` call. Net effect for this file is
 *     unchanged either way: `sx` is safe and correct on both `Flex` and `Stack` here, regardless
 *     of which mechanism is in play.
 *
 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.2): `details`'s desktop gap now branches on `hasError` — 12px
 * (`var(--zimm-scale-s)`) by default, widening to 16px (`var(--zimm-scale-m)`) when an
 * error-variant ZimmInlineMessage is present, per `.claude/session-notes.md` §11.2 ("In error
 * states the Item Details gap widens 12 -> 16px"). Only the desktop step changes — the mobile
 * gap (24px, `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`) is untouched: the design record only calls out the desktop
 * value, and 24px already exceeds 16px, so there is nothing to "widen" on mobile. `baseStyle` is
 * therefore now a function of `hasError` (see `ZimmCartItemStyleProps` above) rather than the
 * plain object it was through SFCC-270 — `row`/`info` are unchanged and simply ignore the new
 * prop.

  parts: ['row', 'details', 'info'],
  baseStyle: ({ hasError = false }: ZimmCartItemStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
    row: {
      flexDirection: 'row',
      alignItems: 'flex-start',
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px mobile
      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
        alignItems: 'center',
        gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-700)', // 28px desktop
      },
    },
    details: {
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px mobile
      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
        // 16px (var(--zimm-scale-m) = foundation/spacing.ts's `m` = 1rem) when an error-variant
        // message is active, else the existing 12px (var(--zimm-scale-s)) — see this file's own
        // docblock and ZimmCartItemStyleProps above.
        gap: hasError ? 'var(--zimm-scale-m)' : 'var(--zimm-scale-s)',
      },
    },

      flexDirection: 'row',
      justifyContent: 'space-between',
      alignItems: 'flex-end',
      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
        flexDirection: 'column',
        alignItems: 'flex-start',
        justifyContent: 'flex-start',
      },
    },
  }),
};

input.description: Locate the shared cart-item constants file

toolu_01DC7rtmDVNeEU8W7hYjCPfQ.description: Locate the shared cart-item constants file

content.content:
1	/**
2	 * Shared constants for the SFCC-11 cart build. Same role as theme/components/footerShared.ts /
3	 * headerShared.ts — see .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "Cross-file shared values" section:
4	 * a value needed by more than one file goes here once, imported everywhere it's needed, so two
5	 * call sites can't independently retype the same number and silently drift apart. Placed
6	 * alongside `ui-kits/` (rather than `theme/components/`, where footerShared.ts/headerShared.ts
7	 * live) because this cart build's first consumer is a component-local recipe co-located under
8	 * `ui-kits/molecules/`, not a `theme/components/`-resident recipe — later commits in this same
9	 * build may add more cart-item constants here, but that is not yet built and is not asserted as
10	 * done by this comment.
11	 */
12	
13	// Icon-button disabled opacity for the cart quantity stepper (ZimmQuantityStepper, SFCC-271).
14	// Intentionally the SAME numeric value as zimmButton.css.ts's own OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED (0.4,
15	// see that file's `icon`/`iconInverse` variants) — not imported from there, because that file is
16	// a Tier 2 recipe this build step does not touch, and a constant needed by a sibling recipe
17	// (zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts) plus this component's own tests should not have to reach into an
18	// unrelated atom's styling module for an unrelated number. Kept here as its own named constant,
19	// deliberately equal, so both places that dim something to "the disabled look" (ZimmButton's own
20	// icon variant, applied automatically once ariaDisabled is passed, and this stepper's own value
21	// display, which is not a ZimmButton and so has no such variant of its own) render at the
22	// identical opacity instead of two independently-authored numbers that only start out matching.
23	// Per conventions.md > "No magic numbers or strings" — a named constant, not an inline literal.
24	export const OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED = 0.4;
25

input.message: ## Scale Ran the 8 priorities the brief specified (mutation-tested the wrapper, real-browser-proved the live region, real-DOM-proved the cap/floor, live-Storybook-proved all 6 stories render, diffed BonusProductQuantity, ran ZimmQuantityStepper's own suite standalone, verified the 5 updated tests are meaningful, confirmed the picker is dead) plus the standing angles that still apply (tokens, styling conformance, structure, imports, accessibility, against-the-ticket, intra-step DRY, story-interactivity-fidelity, React logic correctness). Dropped three sub-checks as vacuous, stated below, not silently skipped: recipe-state-exhaustiveness/hover-gating (no `.css.ts` touched this step), stacking-context/z-index lift-list (`product-item` has no stretched-link overlay — grepped, zero matches), and the text-overflow/geometric-alignment half of real-rendered-layout (this step introduces no new text content and claims no new cross-element alignment). Five sub-agents dispatched (one per angle-cluster), sequenced so the one mutation-testing agent ran alone first and finished/restored before the four read-only/live-render agents ran in parallel — avoided racing a file-mutation against Storybook-dependent checks. I independently re-ran `tsc --noEmit` (clean), the full suite (95 files/1331 tests, matches Marcel's number exactly, fresh not trusted), and `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6/6) myself rather than only trusting secondhand claims. --- ## Priority 1 — Mutation-preservation wrapper (highest value) **CONFIRMED, real regression caught, with one real gap in the guard's own coverage.** Mutated `handleStepperQuantityChange` to the exact wrong-shortcut (`setQuantity(nextQuantity)` directly, bypassing `onItemQuantityChange`), ran the real suite, restored byte-exact (verified via md5 `583cc2fe6b4bcb3277e6fa93d8c99ede` before/after and identical diff-stat), re-ran to confirm clean. **4 of the 5 new mutation-preservation tests failed immediately** under the mutation (`AssertionError: expected "spy" to be called with arguments: [3] / Number of calls: 0` — exactly the predicted mechanism: the spy is never touched). Baseline and final: 19/19 passed both times. 🟡 **`overrides/app/components/product-item/index.test.tsx` — "a synchronous (non-Promise) onItemQuantityChange also works via increment" (in the `handleStepperQuantityChange` describe block) is mutation-blind.** It only asserts `not.toThrow()` and that `setQuantity` is eventually called with `3` — it never asserts `onItemQuantityChange` was called at all, so the wrong-shortcut version satisfies both assertions trivially. This is the one test in a 5-test block whose stated purpose is proving the mutation survives, and it doesn't actually prove that for its own scenario. **CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF** (an isolated missing assertion, not a repeated pattern — the other 4 tests in the same block correctly assert `onItemQuantityChange` was called). Fix is one line: add `expect(onItemQuantityChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith(3)`. 🔵 Two pre-existing tests are also mutation-blind but for benign, non-defective reasons (Agent A traced both): the "omitting onItemQuantityChange" test only checks `not.toThrow()`, and the two boundary tests' `not.toHaveBeenCalled()` assertions fire at a point where `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own `incrementInert` guard stops the click before the mutated code is ever reached, mutated or not. Not findings, noted for completeness. React logic correctness (read-only, no mutation): `handleStepperQuantityChange` is a plain `const`, recreated every render — no memoization, so no stale-closure risk on `onItemQuantityChange`/`setQuantity`. It never reads `product-item`'s own `quantity` at all — `ZimmQuantityStepper` computes `quantity ± 1` itself and hands the wrapper an already-computed value (confirmed by reading `zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx`'s `handleDecrement`/`handleIncrement`), so there's no stale-`quantity` path in this function. `stepQuantity` is no longer destructured anywhere in `product-item/index.tsx` (confirmed via grep) — clean removal, not a dead variable. **CONFIRMED clean.** ## Priority 2 — Live-region proof (Marcel wanted a real answer) **CONFIRMED, end-to-end, via real Chromium against the live Storybook.** Same physical DOM node's `textContent` moved `1→2→3→(blocked, stays 3)→2` across five real clicks on the real accessible buttons, through the real unmocked `useDerivedProduct` hook and the real `handleStepperQuantityChange` promise chain — not markup presence, not a snapshot. Node identity was independently re-verified after all interactions via `page.evaluate(([a,b]) => a === b, ...)` returning `true` (a fresh query resolved to the *same* element, not a lookalike replacement), and `document.contains(el)` stayed `true` throughout. Zero `pageerror` events; the only two console lines were pre-documented inert noise (React DevTools banner, `StoreLocatorProvider` PropTypes warning already called out in the story file's own docblock). Two full runs were byte-identical. 🔵 Real gotcha worth recording for future work on this component (not a defect): the Default story's DOM has **three** `span[aria-live="polite"]` elements — two are `CartItemVariantPrice`'s hidden sr-only price announcements (`aria-atomic="true"`), only one (no `aria-atomic`) is the real stepper value. A naive selector grabs the wrong one. Both Agent B and Agent C independently hit and worked around this the same way, corroborating each other. 🔵 Disclosed, not swept under the rug: the first two script attempts hit the increment button already `aria-disabled` at mount for no apparent reason and hung; two subsequent clean runs were reproducible and consistent. Reads as a transient dev-server/HMR race, not a component defect — flagging in case it recurs, root cause not chased further since it's orthogonal. ## Priority 3 & 4 — Cap/floor enforcement and Storybook stories render, via real DOM **CONFIRMED**, live, through the real unmocked hook chain — stronger evidence than the Implementer's own mocked-hook Vitest tests, per Marcel's ask. Real observed sequence on the Default story: decrement `aria-disabled="true"` at quantity 1 (floor), forced click leaves it at 1; increment `aria-disabled` absent (not `"false"` — the attribute is genuinely omitted, matching `ZimmButton`'s `ariaDisabled || undefined` pattern) through 1→2→3, becomes `"true"` at 3, forced click leaves it at 3 (fallback cap enforced live). All 6 stories (`Default`, `MultipleItems`, `GiftCard`, `WithErrorMessage`, `WithWarningMessage`, `WithDiscountLabel`) render with zero `pageerror`s and no error overlay; `GiftCard` correctly shows **zero** stepper buttons (confirms `hideStepperAndActions` still suppresses the new stepper, not just the old one). 🟡 **Real gap, low severity: pass criterion 2 (`c_maxOrderQuantity: 5` → cap of 5) has zero live/Storybook coverage.** Neither of `index.stories.tsx`'s two mock products sets `c_maxOrderQuantity` (confirmed via grep — zero matches), so every story exercises the fallback-of-3 path only. Someone doing exactly the audit method that caught the original orphaned-component bug (clicking through Storybook) cannot see the override behavior at all today. **CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — the general shape (a prop-driven numeric variant with no representative story) could recur for any future per-product override. Severity kept at should-fix, not must-fix, because the actual risk is narrow: the number-resolution logic has its own thorough mutation-tested unit suite (`maxOrderQuantity.test.ts`), the component-level threading is covered by mocked-hook tests, and the wiring is one unconditional `max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}` with no branch that could treat 3 differently from 5. Recommend a `WithHigherMaxOrderQuantity` story as a cheap follow-up, not a blocker. Story interactivity fidelity (Priority 9 in the standing set): **CONFIRMED genuine**, not the "looks interactive, structurally static" defect — there's no `argTypes`/Controls wiring for quantity at all; the 1→2→3→(clamped) sequence is only possible if the real `useDerivedProduct` state is firing on each real click. ## Priority 5 — `BonusProductQuantity` branch untouched **CONFIRMED**, independently, by two agents reading the same diff hunk: the `product.bonusProductLineItem ? () : (...)` ternary shows zero `+`/`-` markers on the true branch — only the false branch (picker→stepper swap) changed. ## Priority 6 — `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own suite untouched and still passing **CONFIRMED.** `git status --short` on that whole folder is empty; `npx vitest run` on its `index.test.tsx` directly: **17/17 passed**. ## Priority 7 — The 5 updated tests are meaningful, not coincidental **CONFIRMED.** All 5 updated spots located and checked: 3 are hard `getByRole` assertions (fail loud if wrong), the 1 negative (`queryByRole`) assertion is proven non-vacuous by cross-reference to a sibling test using the identical selector successfully. The accessible names were traced all the way to the DOM, not just string-matched: `zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx`'s `defineMessages` → `label` prop → `zimmButton/index.tsx:113`'s `` (I independently re-confirmed this exact line myself, matching the sub-agent's claim). ## Priority 8 — `product-quantity-picker.tsx` is dead code for the cart path **CONFIRMED**, independently re-grepped (not trusting the brief's own characterization). Every hit outside the picker's own two files is a comment/docblock, never a live import. Its own orphaned test still passes standalone: 2/2. ## Structure, Imports, Tokens, Styling, Accessibility (structural) All **CONFIRMED clean**, no findings: - Structure: `handleStepperQuantityChange(nextQuantity: number)` explicitly typed, no implicit `any`, no new exported type/component introduced. - Imports: both new lines use the `app/*` alias (registered identically in `tsconfig.json` and `babel.config.js`), zero circularity one level deep, no `../../../..` chains. - Token audit (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`): **0 findings** in `product-item/index.tsx` (it doesn't appear in either the 7 unacknowledged or 52 acknowledged lists) — the 7 real pre-existing violations elsewhere in the repo are unrelated files, not this step's problem. - Styling conformance: no bare token key, no raw hex/px/rem/em, no array-shorthand anywhere in the actual diff lines — this step adds only prop-wiring and a plain callback, no styling props at all. - Accessibility (structural): no `` in the touched lines, no raw `onClick`-bearing non-native element introduced — the only new JSX is a `` composition, and its own two buttons are real `ZimmButton`/`IconButton`s. - Dropped as genuinely vacuous (confirmed, not assumed): no `.css.ts` touched anywhere in the repo; `product-item.css.ts`/`index.tsx` grepped for `::after`/`position: absolute`/`zIndex`/`stretched` — zero matches, so there's no full-card overlay pattern for a stacking-context check to apply to. ## Intra-step DRY 🔵 **`overrides/app/components/product-item/index.test.tsx:128-129`** — `DECREMENT_NAME`/`INCREMENT_NAME` are a third independently-typed copy of `'Decrease quantity'`/`'Increase quantity'`, alongside `zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx`'s real `defineMessages` source and `zimmQuantityStepper/index.test.tsx`'s pre-existing consts (confirmed via `git log --follow` to predate this step by 6 commits). **CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** (this shape will recur the next time anything renders/tests `ZimmQuantityStepper`) — but this step is extending an *already-established* pattern, not inventing a new one, and a drift here fails loud (the `getByRole` query simply stops matching) rather than silently passing wrong. Rated 🔵 not 🟡 for that reason. Worth a shared exported fixture eventually, not urgent. No finding: `min={1}` passed explicitly even though `ZimmQuantityStepper` already defaults to `min=1` internally — read as a deliberate, tested, cart-specific business rule (own AC, own test) rather than an accidental echo of the child's default; falls under this project's own magic-number exception for `1`. ## Against the ticket Plan's 6 pass criteria: all 6 confirmed satisfied, either at the code level (criteria 4, 5) or via real DOM/browser execution (criteria 1, 2's caveat above, 3, 6). One wording mismatch worth noting, not a defect: criterion 6 anticipated stories might need new args added for `min`/`max`/`onDecrement`/`onIncrement` — the actual implementation keeps all four fully internal to `ProductItem` (derived from `product`/existing state), so no story needed anything added. This isn't step 3.5's fault (its own pass criteria never asked for message-wiring, and step 3.2 was explicitly scoped "presentation only, do not wire detection logic"), and I searched plan.md/HANDOFF.md/findings.md for any step that owns this trigger and found none. See "What Marcel is missing" below. --- ## Visual checkpoint brief Storybook `Commerce/ProductItem`, `Default` story (`http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=commerce-productitem--default&viewMode=story`), plus `GiftCard` for the suppression check. Baseline and final: 19/19 passed both times. 🟡 **`overrides/app/components/product-item/index.test.tsx` — "a synchronous (non-Promise) onItemQuantityChange also works via increment" (in the `handleStepperQuantityChange` describe block) is mutation-blind.** It only asserts `not.toThrow()` and that `setQuantity` is eventually called with `3` — it never asserts `onItemQuantityChange` was called at all, so the wrong-shortcut version satisfies both assertions trivially. This is the one test in a 5-test block whose stated purpose is proving the mutation survives, and it doesn't actually prove that for its own scenario. **CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF** (an isolated missing assertion, not a repeated pattern — the other 4 tests in the same block correctly assert `onItemQuantityChange` was called). Fix is one line: add `expect(onItemQuantityChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith(3)`. 🔵 Two pre-existing tests are also mutation-blind but for benign, non-defective reasons (Agent A traced both): the "omitting onItemQuantityChange" test only checks `not.toThrow()`, and the two boundary tests' `not.toHaveBeenCalled()` assertions fire at a point where `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own `incrementInert` guard stops the click before the mutated code is ever reached, mutated or not. Not findings, noted for completeness. React logic correctness (read-only, no mutation): `handleStepperQuantityChange` is a plain `const`, recreated every render — no memoization, so no stale-closure risk on `onItemQuantityChange`/`setQuantity`. It never reads `product-item`'s own `quantity` at all — `ZimmQuantityStepper` computes `quantity ± 1` itself and hands the wrapper an already-computed value (confirmed by reading `zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx`'s `handleDecrement`/`handleIncrement`), so there's no stale-`quantity` path in this function. `stepQuantity` is no longer destructured anywhere in `product-item/index.tsx` (confirmed via grep) — clean removal, not a dead variable. **CONFIRMED clean.** ## Priority 2 — Live-region proof (Marcel wanted a real answer) **CONFIRMED, end-to-end, via real Chromium against the live Storybook.** Same physical DOM node's `textContent` moved `1→2→3→(blocked, stays 3)→2` across five real clicks on the real accessible buttons, through the real unmocked `useDerivedProduct` hook and the real `handleStepperQuantityChange` promise chain — not markup presence, not a snapshot. Node identity was independently re-verified after all interactions via `page.evaluate(([a,b]) => a === b, ...)` returning `true` (a fresh query resolved to the *same* element, not a lookalike replacement), and `document.contains(el)` stayed `true` throughout. Zero `pageerror` events; the only two console lines were pre-documented inert noise (React DevTools banner, `StoreLocatorProvider` PropTypes warning already called out in the story file's own docblock). Two full runs were byte-identical. 🔵 Real gotcha worth recording for future work on this component (not a defect): the Default story's DOM has **three** `span[aria-live="polite"]` elements — two are `CartItemVariantPrice`'s hidden sr-only price announcements (`aria-atomic="true"`), only one (no `aria-atomic`) is the real stepper value. A naive selector grabs the wrong one. Both Agent B and Agent C independently hit and worked around this the same way, corroborating each other. 🔵 Disclosed, not swept under the rug: the first two script attempts hit the increment button already `aria-disabled` at mount for no apparent reason and hung; two subsequent clean runs were reproducible and consistent. Reads as a transient dev-server/HMR race, not a component defect — flagging in case it recurs, root cause not chased further since it's orthogonal. ## Priority 3 & 4 — Cap/floor enforcement and Storybook stories render, via real DOM **CONFIRMED**, live, through the real unmocked hook chain — stronger evidence than the Implementer's own mocked-hook Vitest tests, per Marcel's ask. Real observed sequence on the Default story: decrement `aria-disabled="true"` at quantity 1 (floor), forced click leaves it at 1; increment `aria-disabled` absent (not `"false"` — the attribute is genuinely omitted, matching `ZimmButton`'s `ariaDisabled || undefined` pattern) through 1→2→3, becomes `"true"` at 3, forced click leaves it at 3 (fallback cap enforced live). All 6 stories (`Default`, `MultipleItems`, `GiftCard`, `WithErrorMessage`, `WithWarningMessage`, `WithDiscountLabel`) render with zero `pageerror`s and no error overlay; `GiftCard` correctly shows **zero** stepper buttons (confirms `hideStepperAndActions` still suppresses the new stepper, not just the old one). 🟡 **Real gap, low severity: pass criterion 2 (`c_maxOrderQuantity: 5` → cap of 5) has zero live/Storybook coverage.** Neither of `index.stories.tsx`'s two mock products sets `c_maxOrderQuantity` (confirmed via grep — zero matches), so every story exercises the fallback-of-3 path only. Someone doing exactly the audit method that caught the original orphaned-component bug (clicking through Storybook) cannot see the override behavior at all today. **CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — the general shape (a prop-driven numeric variant with no representative story) could recur for any future per-product override. Severity kept at should-fix, not must-fix, because the actual risk is narrow: the number-resolution logic has its own thorough mutation-tested unit suite (`maxOrderQuantity.test.ts`), the component-level threading is covered by mocked-hook tests, and the wiring is one unconditional `max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}` with no branch that could treat 3 differently from 5. Recommend a `WithHigherMaxOrderQuantity` story as a cheap follow-up, not a blocker. Story interactivity fidelity (Priority 9 in the standing set): **CONFIRMED genuine**, not the "looks interactive, structurally static" defect — there's no `argTypes`/Controls wiring for quantity at all; the 1→2→3→(clamped) sequence is only possible if the real `useDerivedProduct` state is firing on each real click. ## Priority 5 — `BonusProductQuantity` branch untouched **CONFIRMED**, independently, by two agents reading the same diff hunk: the `product.bonusProductLineItem ? () : (...)` ternary shows zero `+`/`-` markers on the true branch — only the false branch (picker→stepper swap) changed. ## Priority 6 — `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own suite untouched and still passing **CONFIRMED.** `git status --short` on that whole folder is empty; `npx vitest run` on its `index.test.tsx` directly: **17/17 passed**. ## Priority 7 — The 5 updated tests are meaningful, not coincidental **CONFIRMED.** All 5 updated spots located and checked: 3 are hard `getByRole` assertions (fail loud if wrong), the 1 negative (`queryByRole`) assertion is proven non-vacuous by cross-reference to a sibling test using the identical selector successfully. The accessible names were traced all the way to the DOM, not just string-matched: `zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx`'s `defineMessages` → `label` prop → `zimmButton/index.tsx:113`'s `` (I independently re-confirmed this exact line myself, matching the sub-agent's claim). ## Priority 8 — `product-quantity-picker.tsx` is dead code for the cart path **CONFIRMED**, independently re-grepped (not trusting the brief's own characterization). Every hit outside the picker's own two files is a comment/docblock, never a live import. Its own orphaned test still passes standalone: 2/2. ## Structure, Imports, Tokens, Styling, Accessibility (structural) All **CONFIRMED clean**, no findings: - Structure: `handleStepperQuantityChange(nextQuantity: number)` explicitly typed, no implicit `any`, no new exported type/component introduced. - Imports: both new lines use the `app/*` alias (registered identically in `tsconfig.json` and `babel.config.js`), zero circularity one level deep, no `../../../..` chains. - Token audit (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`): **0 findings** in `product-item/index.tsx` (it doesn't appear in either the 7 unacknowledged or 52 acknowledged lists) — the 7 real pre-existing violations elsewhere in the repo are unrelated files, not this step's problem. - Styling conformance: no bare token key, no raw hex/px/rem/em, no array-shorthand anywhere in the actual diff lines — this step adds only prop-wiring and a plain callback, no styling props at all. - Accessibility (structural): no `` in the touched lines, no raw `onClick`-bearing non-native element introduced — the only new JSX is a `` composition, and its own two buttons are real `ZimmButton`/`IconButton`s. - Dropped as genuinely vacuous (confirmed, not assumed): no `.css.ts` touched anywhere in the repo; `product-item.css.ts`/`index.tsx` grepped for `::after`/`position: absolute`/`zIndex`/`stretched` — zero matches, so there's no full-card overlay pattern for a stacking-context check to apply to. ## Intra-step DRY 🔵 **`overrides/app/components/product-item/index.test.tsx:128-129`** — `DECREMENT_NAME`/`INCREMENT_NAME` are a third independently-typed copy of `'Decrease quantity'`/`'Increase quantity'`, alongside `zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx`'s real `defineMessages` source and `zimmQuantityStepper/index.test.tsx`'s pre-existing consts (confirmed via `git log --follow` to predate this step by 6 commits). **CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** (this shape will recur the next time anything renders/tests `ZimmQuantityStepper`) — but this step is extending an *already-established* pattern, not inventing a new one, and a drift here fails loud (the `getByRole` query simply stops matching) rather than silently passing wrong. Rated 🔵 not 🟡 for that reason. Worth a shared exported fixture eventually, not urgent. No finding: `min={1}` passed explicitly even though `ZimmQuantityStepper` already defaults to `min=1` internally — read as a deliberate, tested, cart-specific business rule (own AC, own test) rather than an accidental echo of the child's default; falls under this project's own magic-number exception for `1`. ## Against the ticket Plan's 6 pass criteria: all 6 confirmed satisfied, either at the code level (criteria 4, 5) or via real DOM/browser execution (criteria 1, 2's caveat above, 3, 6). One wording mismatch worth noting, not a defect: criterion 6 anticipated stories might need new args added for `min`/`max`/`onDecrement`/`onIncrement` — the actual implementation keeps all four fully internal to `ProductItem` (derived from `product`/existing state), so no story needed anything added. Stronger than the criterion assumed, not a gap. 🔵 **A real, build-wide gap surfaced by cross-referencing the PRD, not a defect of this step**: `.docs/prd/cart.md:28` requires "**Max 3 units per SKU... per order — error displayed if exceeded (CAI-017)**." Step 3.2 already reconciled the *styling* of that message (warning-variant `ZimmInlineMessage`, copy "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size") — but I confirmed by grepping `cartItemMapper.ts` and `product-item/index.tsx` for `message`/`maxOrderQuantity` that **nothing anywhere in the codebase actually triggers that message** when the stepper hits its cap. Today, hitting the max only dims/disables the `+` button — zero accompanying text. This isn't step 3.5's fault (its own pass criteria never asked for message-wiring, and step 3.2 was explicitly scoped "presentation only, do not wire detection logic"), and I searched plan.md/HANDOFF.md/findings.md for any step that owns this trigger and found none. See "What Marcel is missing" below. --- ## Visual checkpoint brief Storybook `Commerce/ProductItem`, `Default` story (`http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=commerce-productitem--default&viewMode=story`), plus `GiftCard` for the suppression check. No Figma node ID could be located for any of these values in `.docs/prd/cart.md` or the plan text — grepped both for `figma.com`/`node-id`, zero matches; flagging as an open question, not omitting the rows. | What to check | Figma node | Expected value | How to verify | |---|---|---|---| | Stepper gap (− / value / +) | not found in docs | 8px (`var(--zimm-scale-xs)`) | DevTools computed `gap` on the stepper's flex root | | Icon touch target, both buttons | plan text says a node literally named "touchTarget" — no ID found | 24×24px (`var(--zimm-scale-xl)` minW/minH) | DevTools computed width/height | | Value number text | not found in docs | 14px / 500 weight / 18px line-height (`body2Strong`), `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` | DevTools computed font-size/weight/line-height/color | | Decrement icon opacity at quantity 1 | not found in docs | 0.4 (dimmed) | DevTools computed `opacity` on the minus button | | Increment icon opacity at quantity 1 or 2 | not found in docs | 1 (full) | DevTools computed `opacity` | | Increment icon opacity at quantity = max | not found in docs | 0.4 (dimmed) | DevTools computed `opacity` | | Value number opacity at either bound | not found in docs | 1 — never dims from hitting min/max alone, only `isUnavailable` (unused this step) dims it | DevTools computed `opacity` on the number span | | Focus-visible ring, tab to either button | not found in docs | `outline: var(--zimm-focus-ring)`, visibly present vs. no outline at rest | Tab key, DevTools computed `outline` | | Details-row gap around stepper, desktop ≥768px | not found in docs | 12px (behavioural) | n/a | Number visibly updates 1→2→3 on real clicks; a screen reader should re-announce each change | Click with VoiceOver/NVDA running — this is the one row a sighted DevTools check can't confirm, see below | --- ## What I tried to falsify - Broke the wrapper's real-mutation contract directly (the exact regression this step exists to prevent) — it was caught, with one real hole in the guard's own coverage (Priority 1 above). - Tried to treat the live region as proven by markup alone and rejected that — required the same DOM node's text to actually change across real clicks, with referential identity re-checked afterward, specifically because that's the exact failure mode of the bug being fixed. - Tried getting Storybook's Controls panel to drive the quantity to check for the "looks interactive, isn't" defect — confirmed no such panel exists for quantity at all; interactivity is 100% real hook state. - Cross-referenced the PRD text independently rather than accepting the plan's own AC framing at face value, which is what surfaced the un-wired max-quantity message gap. - Independently re-ran `tsc --noEmit`, the full suite, and `recipeGuards.test.ts` myself rather
